exposure: Responsive Parenting (RP) intervention received by mothers with their firstborns
outcome: Maternal feeding practices (food to soothe, structure vs. control-based practices, consistent feeding routines, nonresponsive controlling feeding practices, bottle-feeding practices) with secondborn infants
cohort: Healthy singleton secondborn infants (>=36 weeks gestation) of mothers who previously participated in the INSIGHT responsive parenting intervention study with their firstborns.
finding: Mothers who received the RP intervention for their firstborns used more consistent feeding routines and less nonresponsive, controlling feeding practices with their secondborn infants compared to control group mothers.
followup_time: 1 year after birth of the secondborn
